# Spec: kit-tooling

Project: dsh-kit

## kit-tooling.api-facts-are-runnable

A harness fact a shipped plugin depends on must be assertable by a command that exits non-zero when the fact stops holding.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0005
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## kit-tooling.enforcement-is-checked-behaviourally

An invariant the kit enforces with a command is checked by driving the production modules and requiring the wrong verdict to be refused, so an enforcement point never rests on a test name or on output a green run prints anyway.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0009
- checks:
  - command: run: node scripts/check-gate-invariants.mjs (contains "gate invariants ok")

## kit-tooling.every-command-has-an-implementation

A declared verification command names a file that exists, because a command whose implementation is absent enforces nothing while reading as an enforcement point.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0006
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## kit-tooling.rules-name-a-declared-command

A rule the kit claims must name a command the manifest declares and whose implementation exists; a rule with no enforcement point is reported as an unverified claim rather than presented as a constraint.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0006
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## kit-tooling.verification-is-bound-to-the-code

A recorded verification names the code it judged as well as the laws it judged, so a status cannot report a clean, verified project over a tree the gate rejects.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0009
- checks:
  - command: run: node scripts/check-gate-invariants.mjs (contains "gate invariants ok")

## shipped-plugins.ingestion-ratifies-only-a-record-it-wrote

Ingestion puts a decision to the human only after it has written it, and reports rather than mints when the record was not written, no question channel is available, or the answer cannot be read.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0015 (approved by 0020)
- checks: none, and this law says why: The behaviour is asserted by two tests in `scripts/test-ratchet.mjs` — one drives the tool with a supplied judge result and a stub channel and requires an approval, the other drives it with no judge and requires `attempted: false` and no question. No gate-level check binds them yet, because the suite is a single `node --test` invocation that prints TAP rather than a stable marker line; it becomes enforceable when a dedicated invariant script drives the tool into the three fail-closed states and asserts nothing is minted.

## shipped-plugins.no-raw-tool-schemas

A plugin must not register a tool definition whose parameters or output schema was written by hand, because the registry validates those as raw JSON Schema and rejects the author DSL.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0003
- checks:
  - command: run: node scripts/check-portability.mjs

## shipped-plugins.problem-codes-are-declared

Every problem the ratchet emits carries a code from the closed vocabulary in ratchet-schema.mjs; a code invented at a call site is a defect.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0002
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## shipped-plugins.problems-carry-a-subject

A problem record carries a self-contained message and a subject, so a branch can filter on the subject and a reader can act without opening the source.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0002
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## shipped-plugins.reports-are-written-on-failure-too

An operation that produces a report writes it whether it succeeded or failed, because a report that exists only on success cannot record a failure.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0004
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## shipped-plugins.state-records-what-was-judged

A verification records the spec hash it judged, so a later reader can tell whether the code is still verified against the laws in force.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0004
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## shipped-plugins.the-grill-entry-triggers-the-one-question-and-accepts-no-answer

The grill session's consent entry puts the ratchet's own question to the human through the one question channel and exposes no key an answer could travel in, so it is a third entry to the single channel and never a third channel.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0015 (approved by 0020)
- checks:
  - command: run: node scripts/check-consent-surface.mjs (contains "consent surface ok")

## shipped-plugins.the-panel-offers-consent-only-through-the-question-channel

The ADR panel's ratify action puts the ratchet's own question to the human through the harness user-questions seam and produces an approval only when the human selects the approve label, so the overlay is an entry to the one consent channel and never a second one.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0014 (approved by 0016)
- checks: none, and this law says why: The host-side action does not exist yet, so there is nothing to drive. It becomes enforceable when `scripts/check-consent-surface.mjs` exercises the panel surface the way it already exercises the CLI and tool surface — a fixture with a stub question seam that requires an approval record and a transcript on an exact approve, no artifact on a reject or an unreadable answer, and no artifact when the seam is unavailable.

## shipped-plugins.the-panel-records-no-consent-of-its-own

The panel writes no approval record and sets no authorship field, so no path from the overlay turns a record into law without the ratchet's question having been asked and answered.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0014 (approved by 0016)
- checks: none, and this law says why: Same phase as the law above, and enforceable by the same script extension, which must assert that the panel bundle calls no write and that the host action mints nothing without an answered question. Its mechanical half already holds and is asserted today — the bundle reads through `workspaceFiles.list`/`read` and writes nothing — by `node scripts/test-adr-panel.mjs`, which prints `adr panel render ok`.

## shipped-plugins.the-question-seam-is-measured-from-the-panel-host

Whether the panel's host half can reach the Agent-scoped user-questions seam, or needs an agent-side companion, is measured and recorded before the UI is trusted, because the seam is scoped to an agent and the panel is a web-client plugin.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0014 (approved by 0016)
- checks: none, and this law says why: Nothing has been measured yet; this record decides the requirement rather than claiming the result, which would be the assumption the whole feature rests on. It becomes enforceable when a probe in `scripts/probe-dsh-api.mjs` reports the seam's reachability from the chosen host and the measured fact is recorded in `docs/RATCHET-API-FACTS.md` with its reproduction.

## shipped-plugins.tools-use-defineTool

Every tool a shipped plugin registers is built with defineTool, including one that takes no arguments.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0003
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs

## shipped-plugins.writes-are-atomic

A report reaches a reader whole or not at all, so a crash mid-write cannot be mistaken for a gate that failed.

- authority: agent
- decided in: 0004
- checks:
  - command: run: node --test scripts/test-ratchet.mjs
